messages.subject: Latin characters problem
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Rattle on french language doesn't show accentuates letters. In place,
it put a lot of crossed box. And it doesn't show the fourth source
option neither.  There's some format mistake in the menu too.
I try it on two different computers, same thing.

System : Debian sid amd64.
Rattle version 2.6.6 (10 apr 2011).
R version 2.13.1
Rgtk2  version 2.20.14-1.

messages.subject: Re: Latin characters problem
messages.body_plain:
Eureka. I solve it ! Yeehaa (I'm american).
Well it was effectively an UTF-8 coding problem, because my system was
in ISO coding (/etc/default/locale).
So I switch its in UTF-8 by the command (under debian) : dpkg-
reconfigure locales
then I choose fr_FR.UTF-8 instead of fr-FR@euro ISO-8859-15,
then I reboot
then it works !
It works fine, no latin characters problems (with witch the Execute
button action will not works with the Data menu because Data was
translated by Donn[x]es instead of Données) .
So ok, it's fine now.
Maybe a message in the Rattle website for warning unix users to switch
their systems in UTF-8 will be fine too.

Thanks,

(let's Rattle now...)

messages.body_plain:
I like rattle, but I don't use it all the time.  How do I remove it
from automatically attaching when I start R?  There is nothing about
rattle that I see in .Renviron.site

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:

messages.subject: possible reason for installation errors on Windows, saying that a function/DLL is missing
messages.subject_clean: possible reason for installation errors on Windows, saying that a function/DLL is missing
messages.body_plain:
The following may be a solution, if you have only one disk (-
partition) on your computer.

Our team had trouble with the installation of Rattle on Windows. We
installed GTK and read the tips from the Rattle Web page. After the
step
"Geben Sie 'rattle()' ein, um Ihre Daten mischen.
[Vorher gesicherter Workspace wiederhergestellt]"
which means
"type rattle, to mix your Data ..."
the User interface didn't show up. Instead (different) error messages
were shown, saying that a function / DLL (different for two
installations) could not be found. Could be, that also before that
step something was missing.

Many users are reporting very similar errors on the Internet. The
given answers did not help in our case. I think I found a reason to
many of those problems, that I didn't saw reported yet (I'm new to R
and Rattle, so please excuse, if it's already somewhere written down).

The problem existed on machines without a second disk drive or
partition (even with slightly different installation procedures). But
the installation worked on machines with a "d:" disk drive. I tried to
use a directory as virtual network drive and connected it to "d:": The
problems are gone on both of our machines that only have one disk-
partition.

Perhaps there is a hard coded "d:\..." somewhere in the Windows
installation procedure. (?)

messages.subject: Rattle 2.6.7 released: ewkm + advanced plot
messages.body_plain:
I've just released Rattle 2.6.7

It is currently on the master CRAN site and propagating now to the mirrors.

This version adds support for the entropy weighted (subspace) k-means clustering algorithm in the new siatclust package.

Also note the new Advanced Plots option under the Settings menu (off by default) which begins to use ggplot2 and other improved graphics. Still experimental.

Also some improvements to rattleInfo() command.

See http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/rattle/ChangeLog for the full change log.

Regards,
Graham
